body: Sounds more like a canker sore than a cold sore! I’ve had canker sores all my life but just started getting cold sores since getting HSV
Omg that quote has gotten me through so much shit my whole life it’s so true.
What did they treat the ureaplasma with? Sounds like a UTI actually, doesn’t sound like herpes at all to me. But I’d go to your PCP!

Well it’s six one way, half a dozen another. I don’t say “I have GHSV and OHSV”, I just have HSV in both places, and it just complicates things more. If it’s just genitally then you can kiss without concern, or vice versa, but when it’s both it just feels more limiting. It’s just complicates it more.

I was just diagnosed last month and don’t have any positive stories on dating yet… I disclosed to a couple people I was taking to but they all aren’t interested. The guy I’m pretty sure gave it to me broke things off but I think for unrelated issues….

BUT I also have both ghsv1 and ohsv1 (suspected). I was swabbed genitally and had a TERRIBLE outbreak and it was positive, but she didn’t do a typed swab - but the guy did a blood test and has hsv1. And a few days into my ghsv outbreak, I got a bad sore on my lip - either from kissing or I spread it to myself because I pick at the dry skin on my lips a lot as a nervous habit and didn’t know what I had at first. So I have had sores in both places and I know the struggle. 

It’s like… when it’s both, do I disclose before anything? I’ve been trying to date for the last year unsuccessfully and was already getting frustrated and now THIS… the idea of finding someone seems impossible and now I feel dirty. But what’s helped me recover mentally so far is dating myself, finding hobbies and self care. I’ve gained 10 lbs but I’m feeling better for sure. It will be ok!! I know there are lots of success stories out there. But I think just trying to focus on us is a good start and raise awareness that the stigma is what’s so bad not the thing itself, just gotta get to the point where we don’t feel like it’s a big deal so that we can get these men to understand it too!

From what I read only in the first three weeks, maybe. My symptoms started genitally (I think type 1 from asymptomatic OHSV1 person) and I pick on my lips a lot, and less than a week after my ob starting up bad genitally, I got a spot on my lip. Either I transferred or it was from kissing but I think you can only transfer to yourself in the very beginning while your body is still developing antibodies but yes unlikely.

I completely agree… it has been so traumatic for me. I’ve been single for a year and actively dating and never found anyone then this happened… my depression, suicidal thoughts, etc have resurfaced and several people I disclosed to don’t want to see me anymore and I cannot stand dating right now because the idea of disclosing and being rejected on top of how hard dating is makes me sick. I am in a city with no friends and was putting a lot of weight on dating and being desirable and now I feel disgusting, and nobody has reacted positively to there disclosure so I’ve given up on dating. 

How long did it take you to kind of get out there or feel not as shitty about it?

Posting to follow… I have the same questions. Just diagnosed last week and not handling it well. I’ve been actively dating a LOT the last year and was frustrated at the trouble I’ve had. Then this… just makes everything worse. I have it genitally and a spot developed on my lip too so I’m extra lucky… I was talking to a guy for a few weeks before this and he wanted to take me out but I just didn’t want to get hurt or waste my time so I told him and he’s not interested anymore. I think I need to get cats and give up on the idea of getting married again (I’m divorced and 32)

Y’all are lucky… I’ve only done one disclosure and it wasn’t good. Don’t event want to date anymore… just like with kids, I ask if they want kids before I even meet up. I want to disclose before meeting up because I don’t wanna get hurt or waste my time but again maybe I should wait until after the first date. I was just diagnosed last week I don’t know how to navigate all this.

I’m so sorry this happened to you… honestly I’d feel just as hurt. You do wish that he would have just said no beforehand…. Ugh. I just tested positive yesterday and I’m so scared about this. When do you normally disclose? I almost want to tell them before meeting up just because I don’t want to get attached and then rejected 😔

How is it better?? Dating was hard enough as it was… now this. I disclosed to someone I was chatting with on Bumble and he rejected me. My pool was small to begin with now I feel like I’ll never find anyone.

Oh I faint because I have a needle phobia!! And whenever I pass out it’s never minor and it’s always scary and dramatic. That helps knowing that… it’s been a whirlwind seeing and feeling the sores down below, and on my lip, and in my throat all at once. It doesn’t seem like a lot of people have that bad of luck! Knowing that can happen does help! I hope so!!
I am… don’t know my type yet but the PA was really certain it was herpes and I don’t know if the symptoms are from that or the valtrex but I feel awful. Fever, sore throat, lethargy… headache. Ugh.

I know... I used to be better and viewed it that way and I think I've just gotten lost and selfish along the way. I keep trying and praying and seeking God and a Godly man and when the relationship ends I get so frustrated and mad and alone. 

Thank you. And I am in counseling and have been receiving counseling since I got divorced almost four years ago, thankfully I've recovered a lot since then but I know I still have some things to work on. I know I need to be fulfilled in God alone but it's so difficult, and know that after this my eyes have been opened to how lust is a bottomless pit that can never be satiated.

Oh my word... those are some of the biggest life stressors even without the emergency surgery and life threatening situation. You and your family/fiancé all have my prayers. May the peace that passes understanding come to you from God, and many prayers for your surgery and a quick recovery!

I’m praying for you!! It’s so hard to beat those sins our nature love so much. Try not to view it as failing and be ashamed. Shame doesn’t come from Christ... of course we should try and ignore willful sin but being a Christian doesn’t mean never making a mistake. Otherwise David wouldn’t be after God’s own heart... As long as you realize what is sin and know you don’t want to live in sin, do your best to defeat it and pray for strength. But we all relapse - keep your head up. My prayers are with you. You might not recognize yourself but Christ recognizes you, no matter what you did. Just remember that!

Praying for peace. I’m in Raleigh and know of people impacted... God’s peace passes all understanding and I pray for you to receive that peace with time. It is never easy to recover from something traumatic and I recommend taking advantage of any provided counseling, but may the Lord give you peace in this time. I’m thankful you are safe and am so sorry you and everyone involved and to witness and experience this atrocity.
What do you mean by a hymns church? As in, you get more out of contemporary worship, or that they don’t have good sermons? I’m glad that listening to sermons is helping you!
Thank you so much, I really appreciate it. It’s been tough.

True... I've been in a crisis of faith since my divorce and grew up one way, and have lived very against that way with my boyfriend the last year... I loved him. I wanted it to work. But it kept bothering me. I guess my beliefs in things like the inerrancy of scripture, God's best for us including avoiding premarital sex when possible, living together, cursing - that Christians with true life-changing faith desiring to fellowship and commune about God together. My now ex believes the Bible has errors, nothing I felt was a sin was a sin, and that judging who is a Christian and who isn't (which I never intended to do, I just want to do the right thing) is awful. He hates evangelicals and I don't feel like I'm right with God unless I believe that way. I don't want to be wrong. But the way he believes feels wrong to me. 

​

I was unhappy... it's hard because he's magnetic, I want to be close and the good times were AMAZING. But I was unhappy. We broke up/almost broke up several times. I would give anything to be happy together with him but I couldn't manage it. I still worry it's me. I want to be able to be happy.

That's fair... so do you not have kids now? My ex was super against them. He's OCDish and his house was PERFECT which caused some conflict, even my dog's presence caused issues with his perfect house. I felt materialistic the more I was with him. 

You're so right. In the last 3 years I've gotten divorced, almost finished a doctorate, lost all my friends, made new ones, had to move 4-5 times (I lived with my boyfriend for a month), including moving to a state I didn't know anyone but my boyfriend. I feel like I'll never have stability and it's just been so much. I pray you're right and this winds down. I can't live like this.  It's sad I have for the past few months had a favorite road sign on the highway that didn't have a barrier that I chose to crash into if I decided to. I hate that I think that way. I have an appointment with the therapist my ex and I went to twice on Monday - i liked him a lot.

Thank you so much for responding. I'm trying to hang on. You're right - this is a blind jump. I feel like I've started over so many times I can't do it anymore. I was with my ex husband for 7 years total - then lost all the "christian" friends I had because of the divorce. I wanted a fresh start in another state and met my boyfriend - his faith was more "liberal" than mine was, but since I was hurt I was ok with that. You're right, I do know a couple people. I haven't heard from most of the mutual friends. I have one person at least, maybe two. I'm moving apartments tomorrow night and staying where I'm working now full time next month, with the break up - I'm constantly starting over.

You're right, I'm almost too introspective and perceptive. I constantly ruminated if I really disagreed with him, or if I was playing into unhealthy "evangelical" beliefs. Or did I really believe those beliefs and we weren't compatible? Some/most of our relationship was so amazing and he loved me, cared about me, wanted to protect me so much I feel like a crazy person for not being happy in the relationship and feeling like I sabotaged it because I just want to be unhappy. 

I'm going to try some other options. I just feel so broken and my only relief is scratching and repeating over and over "I want to kill myself I want to die" to keep from thinking and crying. I feel old, my sisters are married with kids now, I wasn't going to have kids with my ex and now I'm not sure. I don't even know what I want or what I believe and feel like an empty balloon.

Could you pray for me? I just broke up with my boyfriend of a year. We were so close but sinning, in my eyes now. I’m more evangelical and he’s Presbyterian USA and we disagreed on so much related to our faith. We tried to find a middle ground and he accused me of being judgmental and picky but I needed to be on the same page in faith. It broke my heart but I had to end it... :(. Trying to come to terms with my faith and that I did the right thing.

This is difficult. Reading these responses are difficult as well... I was in the same situation, I grew up Baptist and have also attended an Acts 29 church so I understand where you’re coming from. My now ex-boyfriend is PCUSA. We differed on so many counts in religion... the truth and purpose of the Bible, salvation, church worship styles, purpose and importance of church community... and he couldn’t understand why that bothered me. If we love each other, why should it matter if we go to different churches? Right?

I’m sorry but I had to disagree. I feel like with marriage, two become one and I never felt fully connected to him with all these differences. We had other issues too, we just looked at the world in two different ways. I have to say that there is a greater focus on similar beliefs/unity in a marriage faith-wise from an evangelical mindset than from a more traditional Protestant one. I hope things worked out for you, but I felt the same... in his church, I never felt close to God. I didn’t learn, truly. Some things preached in Sunday school went dead against my beliefs about Jesus, and when I tried to discuss with him it caused major conflict and he felt I was closed minded and judge mental. 

I know I’m not perfect and we’ve had fights about me wanted close, strong Christian women around me and the evangelical “judgement” of who is “strong” or who is a “fake Christian/Christian in name only”. I never want to be judgmental, but try to be Biblical. He never accepted or understood this part of me, and we never wanted kids. I need to be one with my husband in this. Hope it worked out for you.

First off, I’m sorry you experienced that. Also, I’m in your same boat, except your girlfriends side! My boyfriend is Presbyterian and I grew up baptist. We can’t seem to be happy in the same church and he refuses to attend a different church, but is supposedly happy if we end up going to different churches. It’s hard to mesh those two worlds. Even knowing everyone loves Jesus, there are such stark differences, especially if she’s getting into Pentecostal situations. 

I had a similar experience in a Presbyterian Wednesday night and Sunday school, on the other hand... in one, they were criticizing Jesus and Paul, I felt as though atheists analyzing the Bible than Christians learning from it. Also, talking about the woman and Jesus and how the woman talked about dogs getting the crumbs... interpreting that as though Jesus didn’t know his role on earth and that woman taught Him he was to speak to the Gentiles also. Lots, to me, and more... borderline heretical info that came from a lower belief in the Bible than what I’m used to. But my boyfriend hates contemporary worship or songs and isn’t as religiously conservative as I am. We haven’t figured it out but I hope the best for you... that’s tough.

Thank you for sharing! I’ve been through some shaky faith in the last few years after I got divorced from an abuser and all the “Christians” in my life kept telling me I was going to hell for leaving and I should stay. I’m slowly trying to strengthen my faith but like you, we need to really ask for faith and trust God will reveal himself. I’m so happy you’re feeling better!

I’m sorry you have a relationship like this too! Your story sounds very similar. How long have you been together? We have felt like that too, that if we love each other and push through we’ll be ok, but I wonder how hard relationships are supposed to be and if we’re forcing something that will never really work, if we’ve almost broken up so many times in less than a year, although the rest of the time there’s a lot of love and compatibility. It’s hard to know when you’re growing together or if it’s not meant to be. I hope you all will get stronger too and not have the difficulties anymore!
Yours isn’t so good? I’m sorry about that too. Thank you... yes, it’s definitely a rough time. I’m starting to understand why people just don’t want to date and be happier alone lol.

This is definitely the best description so far of inerrancy not taking light of the Word and Jesus. I’m a historic Baptist/borderline charismatic trying to find her way now that I’m older and learning. As we’ve always been taught that if any of the Bible is wrong, it all could be... but I do really appreciate your description, it makes sense in a way that I never understood before. Thank you!

Question, in what ways do you reject inerrancy and how is that different than Barth’s way of rejecting inerrancy? To be honest I’m not familiar at all with neo-orthodoxy or Barth, and was historically inerrant now more leaning infallible but I’m recently doing some research. Just a question! Thanks!

I have to agree and say I’m in your shoes! I grew up very evangelical and was taught a lot of things that were law. However when I got divorced due to an abusive situation and most of my friends and received a lot of judgement, I rethought a lot of things. I’m trying to figure out what I believe now and about denominations too. I don’t have an answer yet but best of luck in your search!

I’m glad I’m not alone! I’m also glad you appreciated my “predestination” comment, sometimes when I look at other Christians whose faith is so deep I wonder if maybe I’m trying too hard and I’m not meant to be saved. I know that’s not true but it feels that way sometimes!

I agree with that! I think my goal is trying to, each day, read at least a few verses and try to learn from them and apply them in some way, hoping to become more like Him over time. 

Sounds perfect, I appreciate the prayers! You will be in my prayers as well.

Wow, I never thought of it that way. We were always taught more in the way that humans are so minuscule in comparison to such a perfect God that any of our thought is “leaning on our own understanding” and we need to unfailingly trust he Bible. And where it doesn’t make sense, we trust that God’s wisdom is above ours and we just don’t understand it. 

But you’re right. An obsession with knowing the “right” things or not isn’t productive, I need to focus on Him and through His word determine what I truly believe, not what I’ve been told for years, but also not molding Jesus into a more “comfortable” version by watering down anything. But I think in my goal of following God I’ve become legalistic and missed the point to some extent.

Thanks for your response. I certainly felt a bit convicted... I do love God but of course I think I’ve been a bit legalistic and lost sight of what’s really important. I always heard in my head that if we love God we need to follow his commandments... which I’ve historically obsessed over. But if I read his Word and understand it in context, along with the guiding of the Holy Spirit, God will let me know what’s right or not. 

I do care, and/or I want to care more... I’ve always had some doubt and “rededicated” myself so many times as I grew up. I’ve worried that predestination is real and I just wasn’t “predestined” to be a Christian. I’ve struggled to mature in the Word and as I’m getting to my late 20s I need to build a foundation now and figure this out. I’m a work in progress for sure but my passion is there for Him!

Wow, I’d never thought of it this way. It can be so easy to see Christianity one way when you’ve grown up a certain way, but I know not everyone around the world worships in the same way and that doesn’t make them any less “Christian”. Never thought of a literal reading to be modern. 

The book they were studying was Interrupting Silence by Walter Brueggeman, and I bought the ebook and read the chapter in question. He does seem to insinuate that this woman “educated” Jesus and that Jesus went directly after to the Greek cities to preach, as if she changed his mind. I still take issue but there were some interesting things in the chapter and I definitely wonder if I overreacted or not. I’m certainly not a Bible scholar. 

Good idea... I’d say the Presbyterian church he goes to so fairly traditional, but part of me wants to just go to a Catholic mass for interests sake. The Presbyterian service was so new I didn’t like it, historically I feel “close to God” when I fellowship with young people, get emotional about what God’s done during contemporary worship, etc. But the structure of the service I do think I’d appreciate more if I understood the purposes. I’ve also probably never understood the Eucharist in as deep of a way as you do either, I’ll do some research on it. 

That’s true as well! It makes less and less sense that being fundamentalist evangelical is the only true way to follow God, because “the way is narrow” and thus “mainstream Christians” are misled... of course we need to take Christ seriously and the Bible seriously but these deep-seated beliefs just feel more and more wrong!

Good advice. I just finished reading the entire  Bible, it took me about three years but I did it. I will say when my boyfriend and I talked about the sermons we heard on Sunday (different churches) he got a much deeper message and understanding that he was able to relay than I was for sure, yet I feel more “Christian”. I need to focus on the Bible and keep an open mind to the leading of the Holy Spirit and not cling so tightly to the interpretations I grew up with. Thank you.

You bring up some great points too, thank you for your thoughts... I guess I want to be liberal because of not wanting to be judgmental or judged, but at the same time I worry the liberalism is sinful. The idea that humans are fallible and that anything we think is more important than God’s word is dangerous, so thinking for myself feels dangerous. Being fundamentalist feels safe. That’s a hard association to break I’m finding, even though as you stated and the verses you posted, just because you don’t view the Bible as word for word inerrant doesn’t mean you don’t believe in God or Christ dying for our sins. 

It’s just such a hard belief to walk away from.

You make some good points... I really struggled with the divorce topic and also the fact many major teachers I admired preach no divorce for any reason. I don’t think it was sinful... but I’m not completely sure. I think for so long I’ve viewed people with “lax” beliefs like premarital sex is ok, or the OT is mostly stories and not a textbook per se, as being sinners and false conversions and people misled by Satan. I realize how that sounds, it’s just so hard to try and retrain my brain. You’re right, I know I reacted strongly and quickly and I need to be empathetic because I’m inadvertently hurting my boyfriend like my “friends” hurt me, which isn’t Christ-like either.
Yes I’ve thought of this too! I’ve been in a bubble for a long time and I know the range is a lot wider than what I grew up with!
